# @vllnt/convex-notifications

> TypeScript Convex component for in-app notification inboxes: fan-out delivery, read/unread state, unread counts, paginated lists and retention purge.

Install `@vllnt/convex-notifications` (unreleased builds from `main` use the
`canary` dist-tag). Peer dependency `convex@^1.45.0`. Mount it with
`app.use(config)` from `@vllnt/convex-notifications/convex.config` and call it
through `new Notifications(components.notifications, { payloadValidator?, maxFanOut? })`
from host mutations and queries. Methods: `deliver`, `markRead`, `markAllRead`,
`get`, `list`, `unreadCount`, `purge`. `deliver(ctx, subjectRef | subjectRefs, type, payload?)`
writes one unread notification per recipient and returns their minted
`notificationIds`; it is not idempotent and does not deduplicate recipients.
`maxFanOut` defaults to 256 (integer 1 to 500; an invalid value throws
`RangeError` in the constructor). `list` pages newest first, all or
`{ unreadOnly: true }`; views carry `readAt` (absent while unread), not a `read`
flag. `unreadCount` reads a nested `@convex-dev/aggregate`. Pass the
authenticated recipient as `{ subjectRef }` to `markRead` / `get` so another
recipient's id is `NOT_FOUND` / `null`. A typed `Notifications<TPayload>` needs
a `payloadValidator` parser `(value: unknown) => TPayload`. Invalid input throws
`ConvexError` with `data.code` `EMPTY_FANOUT`, `FANOUT_TOO_LARGE`,
`INVALID_MAX_FANOUT`, `INVALID_TYPE`, `INVALID_SUBJECT_REF`, `INVALID_BATCH`,
`INVALID_BEFORE` or `NOT_FOUND`. `markAllRead` and `purge` work in batches
(default 200, 1 to 500) and reschedule themselves. A built-in cron deletes read
notifications created more than 30 days ago every 24 hours; unread ones are never
deleted. The host owns auth, the recipient refs and channels (email, push); there
is no React entry.

## When to use

- Use it when a server event must reach one or many users' in-app inboxes.
- Use it when the UI needs an unread count and an unread-only list per user.
- Use it when read notifications should be deleted after a retention window.
- Do not use it when you need an activity history with no read state: use
  `@vllnt/convex-events`.
- Do not use it when you need to send email or push: use `@vllnt/convex-email`
  or `@convex-dev/expo-push-notifications`, called from your own code.

## For coding agents

The docs are bundled in the package at `node_modules/@vllnt/convex-notifications/`
and match the installed version. Read them, and the shipped `src/`, before
writing code. The links below to `./` paths are files inside the installed package.
